key_risks.description: Embedded securities losses: held-to-maturity securities carry amortized cost of $74.1B against fair value of $64.6B (a $9.5B unrealized loss). Available-for-sale securities carry net unrealized losses of about $4.4B ($3.3B after tax), with roughly $4.5B of gross losses in positions held 12 months or longer. These losses constrain balance-sheet repositioning and tangible equity if rates stay higher, even though management has no plans to sell and the losses do not hit regulatory capital directly. The filing gives no tangible book value sensitivity to a further rate move.

Capital accretion is not visible in the regulatory ratio. CET1 was 10.8% at both June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, with risk-weighted assets up about 3.3% to $496.5B. First-half common dividends and buybacks absorbed about $2.1B, and the BTIG acquisition added goodwill. Further RWA growth or a higher payout could pressure the ratio.

Credit costs are rising with loan growth. First-half provision for credit losses was $1,114 million vs $1,038 million. Card provisions were $831 million in the first half and card charge-offs run near $446 million a quarter. The allowance assumes a baseline unemployment path with a peak weighted-average rate of 5.9%, which may prove optimistic for a consumer-heavy card book.

Policy risk to card economics: an announced executive order proposing a temporary 10% cap on credit card interest rates could pressure the highest-yielding part of the consumer lending book. Management's quantification of the exposure is not apparent in the filing.

Margin durability and revenue mix. Q2 net interest margin improved to 2.79% (2.78% for six months) on fixed-asset repricing, mix and lower funding costs, but first-half net interest income fell on lower earning assets and lower cash balances. Noninterest income was also hurt in the first half by securities repositioning losses.

Acquisition integration and expense growth. Q2 noninterest expense rose 5.9% to $4,428 million, with marketing and business development up 34%, technology and communications up 12.5% and compensation up 3.3%. BTIG's full cost load and integration spending may not yet be fully reflected, and acquired capital markets revenue flatters the efficiency ratio of 57.1%.

Funding mix shift: short-term borrowings rose to $34.8B from $14.6B at year-end, and financing activities provided $25.4B of cash in the first half. This may raise funding-cost and liquidity sensitivity if wholesale markets tighten.

bull_case: Net income of $2,183 million in Q2 2026 rose from $1,821 million a year earlier, and net income applicable to common shareholders rose to $2,098 million from $1,733 million. Earnings comfortably cover the roughly $2.1B returned to shareholders in the first half.

Net interest margin widened to 2.79% in Q2 from 2.66%, driven by loan growth (average total loans up $27.0B, or 7.1%), better earning asset mix, lower funding costs and fixed-asset repricing. These are structural drivers that keep rolling forward as lower-yielding assets mature.

Positive operating leverage: noninterest income rose 13.7% in Q2 against expense growth of 5.9%, and the efficiency ratio improved to 57.1% from 59.2%. Fee growth is broad-based, with trust and investment management fees up 11.7%, lending and deposit-related fees up 11% and investment products fees up 13%.

The BTIG acquisition adds a capital markets platform (capital markets revenue $512 million vs $315 million), which diversifies earnings away from spread income. The Q2 results also show higher client derivative activity and underwriting fees.

Capital is stable: CET1 was 10.8% at both period ends, while CET1 dollars grew about $1.9B. The unrealized securities losses do not flow through regulatory capital, and management has no plans to sell the securities.
Digital-asset custody and stablecoin initiatives offer longer-term fee optionality as payments and custody revenue scale.
bear_case: First-half net interest income fell 8.4% on lower earning assets, and Q2 net interest income benefited partly from fixed-asset repricing and mix. One quarter of a 2.79% net interest margin does not establish a durable trend, and lower cash balances remain a drag.

Fee growth is partly bought. Capital markets revenue includes the BTIG contribution, so the organic growth rate cannot be separated from the filing. The efficiency ratio is flattered by acquired revenue, while marketing (up 34%) and technology (up 12.5%) expenses are climbing and BTIG's full cost load may not yet be visible.

The embedded securities loss is large: about $9.5B on held-to-maturity and about $4.4B on available-for-sale, with accumulated other comprehensive loss of $7.1B. This limits repositioning flexibility and tangible book value, and repositioning losses already hit first-half fee income.
Retained earnings are not building the regulatory ratio. CET1 was flat at 10.8% as risk-weighted assets grew about 3.3%, leaving little room to raise the payout without eroding capital.

Provisions are rising with loan growth, and card credit costs remain elevated. The reserve assumes a peak unemployment rate of 5.9%, and a proposed 10% card APR cap is an unquantified policy risk to the highest-yielding consumer assets.
Funding mix has shifted toward short-term borrowings, which rose to $34.8B from $14.6B at year-end, adding funding-cost and liquidity sensitivity.

what_to_watch.text:
**Net Interest Margin Durability:** Q2 net interest margin reached 2.79% (2.66% a year earlier), helped by loan growth, mix and fixed-asset repricing, and average loans were up 7.1%. However, first-half net interest income still fell 8.4% on lower earning assets, and lower cash balances were a drag. That said, the year-over-year Q2 widening of 13 bp exceeded the 9 bp six-month widening, which suggests exit-rate momentum, and the consolidated margin is the cleaner anchor than the percentage changes in dollar net interest income.

-> Monitor whether the net interest margin holds at or above 2.79%, the drivers of any further fixed-asset repricing benefit, and trends in average earning assets and funding costs.

**Organic vs. Acquired Fee Growth:** Q2 noninterest income rose $401 million (13.7%) to $3.3B, with trust and investment management fees up 11.7% and capital markets revenue at $512 million vs $315 million. However, the capital markets lift is partly from the BTIG acquisition, and first-half fee income was dragged by securities repositioning losses, so repeatable earnings upside depends on organic strength in trust, card and treasury management. On the other hand, the filing also cites higher client derivative activity, bond underwriting and favorable markets, which are repeatable drivers beyond M&A.

-> Monitor a split of fee growth between BTIG and organic lines, capital markets revenue run-rate and trust fee growth ex-acquisition.

**Operating Leverage After BTIG:** The efficiency ratio improved to 57.1% from 59.2% in Q2, with fee income up $401 million against a $247 million (5.9%) rise in noninterest expense. However, the improvement leans on acquired revenue while marketing is up 34.2%, technology and communications up 12.5% and compensation up 3.3%. Some expense growth figures quoted in segment detail are on far smaller bases than the consolidated figures, so operating leverage should be judged on consolidated numbers and net of provision, which rose $37 million to $538 million on loan growth.

-> Monitor the consolidated efficiency ratio, expense growth ex-BTIG, integration costs and the provision-adjusted pre-tax margin.

**Securities Portfolio and Tangible Equity:** Held-to-maturity securities carry a $9.5B unrealized loss (amortized cost $74.1B vs fair value $64.6B), available-for-sale securities carry about $4.4B of net unrealized losses, and about $4.5B of available-for-sale losses sit in positions held 12 months or longer. Management has no plans to sell and the losses do not reduce CET1 directly. That said, repositioning losses already hit first-half fee income (securities losses of $84 million), and the filing gives no tangible book value sensitivity to further rate moves.

-> Monitor accumulated other comprehensive loss, any further securities repositioning, and management commentary on tangible book value sensitivity.

**Credit Costs and Card Policy Risk:** The first-half provision was $1,114 million vs $1,038 million, driven by loan growth, while Q2 net charge-offs eased to $536 million from $554 million and the allowance reflects improved credit quality. However, card provisions remain elevated at $831 million for the half, the reserve assumes a peak weighted-average unemployment rate of 5.9%, and a proposed temporary 10% card APR cap is not quantified in the filing.

-> Monitor net charge-off ratios, card reserve coverage, macro scenario assumptions and any management sizing of APR cap exposure.

**Capital Generation and Shareholder Returns:** First-half common dividends of about $1.6B and treasury purchases of $0.5B totaled roughly $2.1B, about 53% of net income applicable to common, so earnings cover the payout. However, CET1 held at 10.8% as risk-weighted assets rose from $480.4B to $496.5B and BTIG added goodwill, so retained earnings of about $1.8B are being absorbed by growth. On the other hand, CET1 dollars grew about $1.9B, so the flat ratio is mostly arithmetic rather than a generation failure.

-> Monitor the CET1 ratio, risk-weighted asset growth split between BTIG and organic loans, and buyback pace.

**Digital-Asset and Payments Fee Optionality:** Fee revenue grew 13.2% in Q2, and recent news shows custody of stablecoin reserves for a digital bank and a cross-border stablecoin payment test. However, the magnitude is unproven: the stablecoin items come from news rather than the filing, and part of the fee growth was acquired through BTIG.

-> Monitor any disclosure of digital-asset revenue, custody balances and payments-segment fee trends.

**Funding Mix and Balance-Sheet Growth:** Net loans rose to $402.7B from $383.7B at year-end, and short-term borrowings rose to $34.8B from $14.6B while deposits grew by $10.0B in the first half. However, the heavier reliance on short-term borrowings could raise funding costs and weigh on margin if deposit growth lags loan growth. On the other hand, long-term debt fell to $56.8B from $59.4B.

-> Monitor deposit growth vs loan growth, the short-term borrowing balance and the funding-cost contribution to margin.
